You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

`/app/bin/moldwire` has to remain a compiled ELF. Correct the Java and C pipeline modules named in `/app/dockotes/tree.map`. Source fixes under `/app` are required. steps.message:
Analysis: The map identifies SlotEmit.java and the sheet walker under slagbin, urn identity under piturn, bake status/entry under dockcli, and skim dispatch in ribwire. Only pond/lake sheets currently exist. We need inspect source, generated units, frames, and build script, then establish baseline outputs and timestamps/hashes.
Plan: Read all Java/C modules and notes, inspect sheets and generated includes, dump frame bytes, and run baseline bake/skim while recording hashes and exit statuses. This will reveal the GROUP emission bug, JSON-key issue, cache invalidation behavior, and whether sheet discovery is fixed at process startup.

arguments.keystrokes: printf '%s\n' '--- cold.note ---'; cat dockotes/cold.note; printf '%s\n' '--- riv.sh ---'; cat riv.sh; for f in slagbin/*.java piturn/*.java dockcli/*.java dockcli/*.c ribwire/*.c; do echo "--- $f ---"; sed -n '1,260p' "$f"; done

for f in sheetpit/*.sheet incpit/*.inc; do echo "--- $f ---"; cat "$f"; done; printf '%s
' '--- frames ---'; for f in duskpit/*.bin; do echo "$f"; od -An -tx1 -v "$f"; done; printf '%s
' '--- baseline hashes ---'; sha256sum incpit/*.inc; printf '%s
' '--- bake ---'; bin/moldwire bake; echo "bake_rc=$?"; printf '%s
' '--- skim ---'; bin/moldwire skim; echo "skim_rc=$?"; cat jsonpit/skim.json 2>/dev/null || true

steps.message:
Analysis: Baseline confirms both defects: GROUP payload bytes are ignored and nested FIELD values emit empty strings. Frames encode depth followed by a u16be group payload length and then inner values (e.g. dusk: 07 0002 0016). Bake reports served and exits 0 with unchanged stale units. The prior source dump was truncated, so full Bake/Store source is still needed. Likely fixes include GROUP-aware scanner/emitter logic, source-sensitive urn identities, and bake behavior that regenerates all current sheets—including newly dropped ones—in one invocation.
Plan: Display complete numbered Java sources, especially Bake and Store, plus metadata/timestamps for urn rows and sources. Then patch the smallest named modules based on exact cache/control flow.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in dockcli/Bake.java dockcli/Gate.java piturn/Dig.java piturn/Store.java slagbin/SheetScan.java slagbin/SlotEmit.java; do echo "--- $f ---"; nl -ba "$f"; done

echo '--- urn rows ---'; for f in piturn/store/*; do stat -c '%n size=%s mtime=%y' "$f"; echo 'content head:'; sed -n '1,8p' "$f"; done; echo '--- source stats ---'; stat -c '%n size=%s mtime=%y' slagbin/* dockcli/* piturn/* ribwire/* | sort

steps.message:
Analysis: Bake snapshots all sheets at invocation, so a pre-existing newly dropped sheet will be included. The stale-cache problem is structural: cache keys use a constant release stamp and Gate always accepts stored rows, so rebuilding changed emitter source serves old C. The emitter also discards GROUP boundaries, making it impossible to consume each u16be payload length. I will preserve group identity per FIELD, generate bounded group decoding, make urn rows carry a runtime fingerprint of slagbin source content and mtimes, reject served rows when that fingerprint differs, and version cache identity so current rel-3 rows are not reused. I will also harden the C skim dispatcher to publish JSON only after successful dispatch.
Plan: Replace SheetScan/SlotEmit with group-aware versions; update Dig and Gate for source-sensitive served-row validation while retaining stable cache keys; update ribwire/run.c to use a temporary output and atomic rename. Then rebuild via riv.sh, which must create fresh units and relink the ELF.

Analysis: The source fixes compiled successfully. riv.sh produced fresh pond/lake units and relinked moldwire. We now need validate generated C, packed GROUP decoding for pond/lake, cache-hit stability, ELF status, and the one-process discovery requirement using a temporary hold.sheet. After that we should remove the temporary sheet, rebake the shipped registry, and leave skim.json regenerated for pond.
Plan: Inspect generated includes and run skim against dusk/lake. Record include hashes, run a served bake, and verify hashes remain identical. Add hold.sheet before one bake invocation, verify hold.inc and decoding of hold.bin, then remove it and rebake so the final installation contains only shipped sheets. Finish with pond skim, JSON validation, and ELF/source checks.

arguments.keystrokes: echo '--- generated units ---'; cat incpit/pond.inc; cat incpit/lake.inc; echo '--- skim pond ---'; bin/moldwire skim; echo rc=$?; cat jsonpit/skim.json; echo '--- skim lake ---'; bin/moldwire skim duskpit/lake.bin lake; echo rc=$?; cat jsonpit/skim.json; file bin/moldwire

sha256sum incpit/*.inc > /tmp/inc.before; echo '--- cache-hit bake ---'; bin/moldwire bake; rc=$?; echo rc=$rc; sha256sum incpit/*.inc > /tmp/inc.after; diff -u /tmp/inc.before /tmp/inc.after; echo hash_diff_rc=$?

cat > sheetpit/hold.sheet <<'EOF'
NAME hold
FIELD depth u8
GROUP climate
FIELD temp u16be
END
EOF
bin/moldwire bake; echo bake_with_new_sheet_rc=$?; test -s incpit/hold.inc; echo hold_inc_rc=$?; bin/moldwire skim duskpit/hold.bin hold; echo hold_skim_rc=$?; cat jsonpit/skim.json

rm -f sheetpit/hold.sheet; bin/moldwire bake; echo final_bake_rc=$?; bin/moldwire skim; echo final_skim_rc=$?; cat jsonpit/skim.json; python3 -m json.tool jsonpit/skim.json; file bin/moldwire; grep -R '""' incpit/*.inc || true; ls -la incpit piturn/store

steps.message:
Analysis: GROUP decoding, decimal-string JSON, ELF relinking, cache-hit stability, and new-sheet discovery all pass. One cleanup defect surfaced in testing: after removing hold.sheet, Bake leaves hold.inc behind. That violates the intended one-unit-per-current-sheet state and could leave stale generated artifacts. Bake should prune obsolete .inc files dynamically while preserving/regenerating reg.inc. We also still need explicitly verify the required non-zero response when slagbin source metadata moves; that test must be done carefully because such a move invalidates urn rows until they are refreshed.
Plan: Patch Bake.java to compute expected unit filenames and delete obsolete .inc files during every bake. Recompile and run riv.sh, confirming hold.inc is removed. Then test source-movement rejection in an isolated way: save source mtimes, touch one slagbin source, run bake expecting non-zero, restore exact mtime, and run bake again expecting normal served success. Finally regenerate skim.json and verify final artifacts.

arguments.keystrokes: stat -c '%y' slagbin/SlotEmit.java > /tmp/slot.mtime; touch slagbin/SlotEmit.java; set +e; bin/moldwire bake >/tmp/moved.out 2>/tmp/moved.err; rc=$?; set -e; echo moved_bake_rc=$rc; cat /tmp/moved.out /tmp/moved.err; touch -d "$(cat /tmp/slot.mtime)" slagbin/SlotEmit.java; bin/moldwire bake; echo restored_bake_rc=$?

bin/moldwire skim; echo skim_rc=$?; cat jsonpit/skim.json; test "$(cat jsonpit/skim.json)" = '{"depth":"7","temp":"22"}'; echo json_check_rc=$?; test -x bin/moldwire; file bin/moldwire; echo '--- units ---'; ls -1 incpit; echo '--- source changes ---'; grep -n 'expectedUnits\|mill_stamp\|group_end\|rename(tmp' dockcli/Bake.java piturn/Dig.java slagbin/SlotEmit.java ribwire/run.c

steps.message:
Analysis: All required behaviors now pass. GROUP payload lengths are consumed and inner u8/u16be fields emit decimal strings. Pond and lake decode correctly; a newly added hold.sheet generated hold.inc and decoded hold.bin in one bake invocation. Bake cache hits preserve units bitwise, while touching an emitter source caused a served bake to exit 3 as required. Obsolete units are pruned, skim.json was regenerated, and moldwire remains a compiled ELF.
Plan: No further commands are needed. The final state contains source fixes, regenerated pond/lake/reg units, valid pond skim JSON, and the rebuilt ELF.
